# M42 — the inverse vein: the P361 parents the atlas does not hold

**GENERATED by the fire of 1 October 2026, 23:30Z, and then ticked by hand.**
This is the measurement the batch-86 stand put first among its four candidate
next questions, and the answer to it: every active event's own `P361` (part
of) that is **not** a record of this atlas, with what the item says about
itself and what importing it would do to the main count.

**The question, exactly.** 1,290 of the 1,422 active events carry a Wikidata
item. Their `P361` statements name **301 distinct targets**; **130** are
records here already and **171** are not. Those 171 are the rows below. One
query of `wbgetentities` over 26 chunks asked it, and a second over the 171
read each one's label, description, English sitelink, `P31`, `P361`,
`P17`, dates and point.

**How to read `net`.** The number is what importing that item would do to the
main count: **+1** for the umbrella itself unless one of *its* own `P361`
parents is a record here (then it is filed and adds no main event), minus one
for every held child of it that is **main today**. A6 says the main count must
not rise, so **a row at `net` above 0 is not importable under A6** however
good the article is. A child already filed under something else reduces
nothing — it gains a second parent under A8 and stays off the resting picture
either way.

**What the measurement found.** Of the 171: **137** have an English article,
**162** are not a disambiguation page or a list by their own `P31`, and
**78** clear all three gates at once — an article, a class the table can
classify, and `net` at zero or below. That is the vein's size. It is
**thin for Africa**: six rows have a child in the africa lane and two of those
six are the Cold War and the War on Terrorism, which the stand has ruled out,
so **the lane A10 puts first has four rows in this whole vein**. Asia has
thirty-one.

**`done`** means a record was written for it; **`refused`** means a fire
read it and said no, with the reason in the refusals table at the foot. A row
with neither has not been looked at.

## What this file is not

It is not a queue to walk end to end the way
`docs/m42-umbrella-children.md` was. That vein paid one record per ~144
articles read because its rows were *children* — individual battles and
operations, whose articles had to be read for a sentence. **These rows are
umbrellas**, and an umbrella needs no article read at all to be judged: the
`net` column, the class and the span decide it, and all three are in the
table. A fire takes the rows it wants from the top of its lane and writes
them; the cost is one import call per row, not one article.

The counterpart is that **an umbrella carries no edge**, so this vein cannot
grow the largest connected component. What it moves is the main count, which
is A6's standing demand, and the active count per lane, which is A10's.
